subject.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic refusal and OpenAI content_filter as failover-eligible refusals

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off generic refusal fallback policy for provider safety/content-filter refusals after the code/proof gaps are fixed?
rationale: Even with the default off, the config creates an operator-controlled path that can send a provider-blocked prompt to another model or provider with different safety behavior.

options.title: Accept default-off opt-in after fixes
options.body: Allow the config surface once every fallback entry point honors it, docs/tests cover default-off and enabled behavior, and real behavior proof is posted.

options.title: Keep generic refusal fallback out
options.body: Rely on provider-sanctioned fallbacks such as the Anthropic Fable-to-Opus path and keep generic/OpenAI content-filter refusals terminal.

options.title: Narrow to diagnostics first
options.body: Add clearer refusal diagnostics and user copy without automatic model fallback until cross-provider policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Accept default-off opt-in after fixes
recommendation.body: Allow the config surface once every fallback entry point honors it, docs/tests cover default-off and enabled behavior, and real behavior proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged provider-side Anthropic fallback and is the clearest current owner for the remaining generic refusal-fallback policy question.
